ctnh.multiblock.demon_will_generator.shi: Base Generation Formula: Final Power = Concentration Difference * log2(Concentration Difference) * 256 * Diversity
When Specialization Mode is active, the base concentration difference is multiplied by an extra *2, and only the Will of the corresponding specialization is consumed
When Life Essence Boost Mode is active, the final power generation is multiplied by *(2 + 0.25 * Sacrificial Rune Level)

Diversity affects power generation efficiency and is calculated according to the Simpson Diversity Index. It is 0.2 when there is only one type of Will, up to a maximum of 1, and fixed at 0.8 when Specialization Augment is active.

Each time Demon Will transfers, it consumes 8% of Demon Will from one side and grants half of the consumed amount to the other side. When the amount of Demon Will is <10, all Demon Will will be consumed at once and no transfer will occur.
ctnh.multiblock.demon_will_generator.too: Allows using laser hatch, substation hatch

Generates power using the concentration difference of Demon Will between the chunks on both sides of the machine. The larger the concentration difference, the more the power generation grows exponentially.
Calculations are based on the Will concentration at the Demon Alloy Blocks on both sides of the machine.
The diversity of various types of Demon Will within the chunks on both sides affects power generation efficiency.
Placing a Will Core inside the machine switches it to Specialization Mode, targeting only a specific type of Will.

Rune blocks inside the machine can be replaced to provide different upgrades:
§4Rune of Sacrifice and Rune of Self-Sacrifice§r----Boosts power multiplier in Bewildered Amplification Mode (2+0.25*Rune Level)§r
§3Rune of Velocity§r----Increases recipe duration (+20% per level)§r
§eRune of Augmented Capacity§r----Each rune adds +2 to the Demon Will concentration difference§r
§cRune of Superior Capacity§r----Each rune multiplies the Demon Will concentration difference by an extra *1.2 (multiplicative)§r
==============================
Input §4Bewildered Fluid§r to activate Boost Mode, consuming 1000mb of Bewildered Fluid per second.
Hold Left Ctrl to view detailed formula

ctnhmana.spire.page.1: The Mystic Spire is an advanced structure that you can craft after defeating Gaia. It generates §bDelta Sparks§r, an advanced special variant of Sparks.$(p) The Mystic Spire can replace traditional spreaders and sparks to supply mana to various mana containers (including Mana Condensation Hatches).$(br)For specific working logic, please refer to the entry: Delta Spark
ctnhmana.spire.page.2: When the Mystic Spire structure is complete, it generates a §bDelta Spark§r and binds with it. If the Mystic Spire structure becomes invalid, the §bDelta Spark§r disappears, but the data is retained in the spire master block.$(p) Toggle the mode of the spire/spark to determine the working mode of the Mystic Spire. A §bDelta Spark§r can bind to another §bDelta Spark§r, transferring mana to it regardless of the mode; this effect is independent of transfer speed calculations and ignores mode restrictions.
ctnhmana.spire.page.3: The Mystic Spire has multiple modes. You can switch them in the machine master block UI, or use a §bStaff of the Digital Elf§r in operation mode on the Mystic Spire/Delta Spark to switch modes.$(p) The Mystic Spire currently has four modes: §4Focus, §cSpark Diffusion, §bWide-Area Diffusion, §6Transfer
ctnhmana.spire.page.4: Various attributes of the Mystic Spire determine the performance of the Delta Spark:$(p)Speed: Determines the speed at which the spark transfers mana, initial value 10,000/tick$(p) Receiving Speed: Determines the speed at which the spark actively absorbs mana. Note that the spark's initial absorption rate from mana-generating flowers is only 1/10 of the receiving speed, initial value: 10,000/tick$(p)Range: Determines the spark's area of effect, initial value: 15
ctnhmana.spire.page.5: The Mystic Spire's mode determines its working logic:$(p)§4Focus§r: The Mystic Spire does not output mana, but automatically accepts mana from surrounding sparks of the same color or mana-generating flowers.$(p)§cSpark Diffusion§r: The Mystic Spire outputs mana to surrounding sparks of the same color and mana condensation hatches with spark upgrades.$(p)§bWide-Area Diffusion§r: The spark ignores all restriction rules and transfers mana to all surrounding non-Delta Spark mana containers.$(p)§6Transfer§r: The Mystic Spire does not perform any operations, it only facilitates mana transfer between Mystic Spires.
ctnhmana.spire.page.6: Mystic Spires can be bound together using the §4Staff of the Digital Elf§r.$(p)In the binding mode of the §4Staff of the Digital Elf§r, the first right-click on a Delta Spark selects the target spark to bind, and the second completes the binding, causing the Mystic Spire to transfer mana to the target spark.$(p)Use shift+right-click on a Delta Spark to clear the binding. Note: Cyclic transfer loops between Mystic Spires are allowed.
ctnhmana.spire.page.7: The Mystic Spire comes with four upgrade slots, where upgrades can be freely installed to increase various attributes of the spire. However, note the following:$(p)Dislocation upgrades for absorbing mana-generating flower efficiency only take the maximum value$(p)The maximum range of the Mystic Spire is 50, maximum capacity is INT_MAX, and the maximum transmission speed cannot exceed 1/10 of the maximum capacity

The 24 Solar Terms is an ancient Chinese calendar system used to guide agricultural affairs, reflecting natural phenomena and farming seasons in the Yellow River basin. It is the crystallization of long-term experience and wisdom, inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2016.
Chushu (End of Heat): The end of the summer heat.
Xiaohan (Minor Cold) and Dahan (Major Cold): The degree of coldness in winter.
Guyu (Grain Rain): Rain brings growth to hundreds of grains.
Bailu (White Dew), Hanlu (Cold Dew), and Shuangjiang (Frost's Descent): Temperatures fall, and moisture condenses.
Xiaoxue (Minor Snow) and Daxue (Major Snow): The degree of snowfall.
Jingzhe (Awakening of Insects): Spring thunder wakes hibernating animals.
Qingming (Pure Brightness): The weather turns clear, and plants sprout.
Xiaoman (Grain Buds): Grains of cereal crops begin to plump.
Mangzhong (Grain in Ear): Grains with awns (like wheat) ripen.
The 24 Solar Terms are divided based on the sun's position along the ecliptic (Earth's orbit around the sun) every 15°. There are 24 terms in a year, split into four categories:
Lichun (Beginning of Spring), Lixia (Beginning of Summer), Liqiu (Beginning of Autumn), and Lidong (Beginning of Winter): The start of the four seasons.
Chunfen (Spring Equinox) and Qiufen (Autumn Equinox): Day and night are of equal length.
Xiazhi (Summer Solstice) and Dongzhi (Winter Solstice): The longest day and shortest day of the year.
Xiaoshu (Minor Heat) and Dashu (Major Heat): The severity of summer heat.

When the machine's voltage tier is higher than required by the recipe, it triggers &eoverclocking&r, consuming extra power to speed up execution. Each tier above the required level adds one overclocking step.

Standard overclocking is &blossy overclocking&r: the EU consumed per tick increases by 4x, but the processing time is only cut in half. For example, if an &bMV&r machine runs a 10-second &7LV&r recipe, lossy overclocking increases power consumption from 1A &7LV&r to 1A &bMV&r (4x), and cuts recipe duration to 5 seconds (2x speed). In this case, the total energy (EU) consumed is doubled, making it "lossy".

In some cases, &alossless overclocking&r is triggered: power consumption increases by 4x, but the duration is cut to 1/4. Here, the total EU consumed remains unchanged, making it "lossless". Machines with lossless overclocking will mention it in their tooltips.

When multiple overclocks are triggered, they compound. If an &5EV&r machine runs an &7LV&r recipe, triggering three steps of lossy overclocking, the EU/tick consumption becomes 4x4x4=64x, while the processing time is cut to 1/(2x2x2)=1/8.
&bNote&r: For &8ULV&r-tier recipes, the compound overclocking count is always reduced by one.

&e   Electricity (GTEU)&r is another recipe input/output. Most machine recipes consume EU, while generators produce EU, which can be transmitted via wires and cables. Unlike items or fluids, EU is not consumed all at once at the start of a recipe; it is consumed continuously every single tick.

If you attempt to speed up a machine by any means, its EU consumption rate will also double. However, single-block machines have an input current limit of 2A; over-accelerating will lead to power shortages (usually causing the machine to lose power if speed exceeds 2x). Placing a battery directly in the machine's battery slot provides power without any rate limit, allowing you to speed it up as much as you like.
For &bmultiblocks&r, power is supplied via Energy Input Hatches, and generators output electricity via Energy Output Hatches.

GregTech recipes requiring electricity have specific &evoltage tiers&r, which can be identified by the voltage icon in the bottom-right corner or the border color in EMI. If a machine's voltage tier is lower than the recipe's requirement, the machine &4cannot&r run that recipe, even if it has access to plenty of EU.
For single-block machines (referred to as &bsingle-blocks&r), the tier corresponds directly to the rated input voltage in their description.
For multiblock structures (referred to as &bmultiblocks&r), the tier is determined by the Energy Hatches installed. If hatches of different tiers are used, the highest tier takes precedence.

Almost all raw GregTech ores go through four basic processing stages: Macerating, Ore Washing, Thermal Centrifuging, and Centrifuging. Some gemstone ores can also be sifted, and certain ores can undergo chemical leaching or magnetic separation. Different processing paths yield different byproducts; choose the path that best suits your current needs.
Only Macerators at HV tier or higher yield byproducts; the Crushing Factory does not produce byproducts.
Unlike most tech mods that use &2FE&r, GregTech machines run on GTEU, commonly referred to as &eEU&r.

Much like real-world electricity, EU transmission involves the concepts of Voltage (measured in &eV&r) and Amperage (measured in &eA&r). A current of 1V and 1A transmits exactly 1 EU per tick. (A tick is the basic time unit in Minecraft; under normal conditions, 1 second equals 20 ticks, abbreviated as t).
EU can be converted into FE automatically, meaning you can power FE-compatible machines by feeding them EU directly.
Converting FE to EU requires power converters. Note that &4converters above LV tier have been disabled in this modpack&r.

A &eRecipe&r is a fundamental concept in Minecraft and lies at the heart of the gameplay. Generally, a recipe consists of the following key elements:
&b   Inputs (or Ingredients)&r: The materials required, such as Diamonds to craft a Diamond Block, or raw beef to cook a steak.
&b   Outputs (or Products)&r: The resulting items produced by the recipe.

&b   Processing Time&r: Crafting table recipes finish instantly, but furnaces and most GregTech machines require time to process inputs into outputs. &mSo essentially, all GregTech machines are just glorified furnaces.&r

&b   Recipe Conditions&r: Requirements for the recipe to execute, such as requiring Blaze Burner heat for a Create Mixer recipe. In a way, conditions act as inputs, but they aren't consumed during the process.

As you advance your technology, you will continuously encounter new ingredients, products, conditions, and processing times. The following quests will cover the most important points. If they seem confusing now, feel free to refer back to them later when you encounter them.

Overview: ME Storage Network technology (referred to as ME Network below) is a technology that converts physical items into data inside ME drives via terminals, ME interfaces, and ME buses, and can materialize them back into physical items through the same channels.

Terminology Explanations:
1. Channels: The limit on the number of channel-consuming devices that can connect to the ME network. An ad-hoc network without an ME Controller can connect up to 8 channel-consuming devices. An ME Controller block provides 32 channels per face (unlocked at HV tier). Multiple controller blocks can connect to form a larger cluster for more channels, but the channels per face remain constant. Only one ME Controller cluster (a contiguous multiblock structure not exceeding 7x7x7) can exist in a single ME network.

ME Glass Cables and ME Smart Cables can only transmit 8 channels, while ME Dense Cables can transmit 32 channels. Because of this, standard Smart Cables cannot fully extract all channels from a single face of an ME Controller, which is why P2P Tunnels are essential (see https://ae-2.wiki/ for more details).
2. P2P: See official documentation on ME P2P Tunnels.
3. AE Power: Power requirements and energy networks.
4. Autocrafting Guide: Refer to online resources or guides.

kubejs.ponder.assembly_line_building.hea: How to build a gregtech multiblock
kubejs.ponder.assembly_line_building.tex: First, you need a assembly line main block.
Place the storage part of the AE subnet.
Please note that quartz fiber should be used to disconnect the direct connection between the subnet and the main network, while also supplying power to the subnet.
Set the priority of the storage bus, decreasing from the main block direction to the output bus, which means whether your materials will enter the assembly line in the correct order for synthesis.
Place the 'one click template' ('+'button) in the template encoding terminal of the pattern provide to ensure that the materials are output to the buffer in the correct order.
Change the lock synthesis mode to 'until the main product is returned' on the left side of the pattern provide.
Put in the research data required for the formula
Congratulations, you have learned how to use AE2 for assembly line automation.
One click placement using the terminal.
Place the pattern provider in the AE main network, paying attention to place to closely to the ULV output bus.
Use a wrench to adjust the sample supplier to send material upwards.
Place any level of buffer, pay attention to place to closely following the quadruple input hatch.

kubejs.ponder.windmill_control_center_bu: How to build a gregtech multiblock
First, you need a windmill control center main block
One click placement using the terminal.
Place the input hatch to ensure that lubricating oil can be input
Place sufficient kinetic output hatch to ensure that stress can be output.
Place windmill bearings within the 16 grid radius of the main block, and the more they are placed, the more stress they will output. A maximum of 16 windmill bearings can be included.
Connect 128 sails or wool to each windmill bearing to maximize the stress of each windmill bearing.
With sufficient stress output compartment, you can now enjoy the power of the windmill.
